case.description: Design a serviceable retention arrangement for a replaceable flat scraper plate in a dry reciprocating test fixture. The plate and moving carriage already exist; the plate must be removed for inspection without disassembling the carriage.
case.valued_outcome: Retain the plate within 1 mm of its initial position over twenty manual strokes, then permit removal and return within sixty seconds without touching its marked working edge.
hard_constraints: Do not drill, cut, heat or glue the plate or carriage.
Keep the marked 30 mm working edge exposed.
No added part may extend into the marked stroke clearance.
The carriage must remain attached to its rails.
resources: One carriage, one 100 by 60 by 2 mm scraper plate and an identical spare plate.
Four 80 mm steel strips, six M4 bolts with nuts, two small magnets, four cork pads and 0.5 m of wire.
Hand drill for strips only, pliers, screwdriver, ruler and marker.
Eighty minutes of fabrication time and twenty minutes of observation.
observations: An unretained plate moves 6 mm after five strokes.
The carriage has two existing mounting slots outside the stroke clearance.
Awkward observation: the spare plate looks identical but the supplied magnets hold it less strongly; in the supplied pull check it releases at 3 N instead of 7 N.
